- If sentiment is consistently negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward early.
- If sentiment spikes upward (e.g., +1.00) followed by a sharp drop, model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast rise after spike or add lagged correction.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias in mid-to-late horizon.
- If model forecast is rising steadily with no sentiment signal, it often fails to account for upcoming volatility or policy shocks; add volatility buffer or downward adjustment after 10-15 days.
- In cases where true outcome diverges sharply from forecast mid-horizon (e.g., sudden drop after spike), model may be overfitting recent trend; reduce forecast slope after 5-7 days of high momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +1.00 followed by -1.00, model tends to overcorrect; apply smoothing or dampen forecast adjustments after sentiment reversal.
